title: Evidentiary Standard Mismatch Across Regulatory Transitions
scenario_text:
**Maxient Case #IX-2025-0298**
Complainant: Student C | Respondent: Student D
Incident date: March 8, 2025 | Formal complaint filed: September 19, 2025
Hearing scheduled: February 28, 2026 | Status: Investigation complete, pre-hearing phase
Investigator's report (filed Jan 15, 2026): "Applying clear and convincing evidence standard per current BSU Title IX Policy v6.0 (effective August 1, 2025)."

**Google Doc — "BSU Title IX Policy v5.3" (archived, effective Sep 2023 — July 31, 2025)**
Section 8.2: "The standard of evidence for all formal complaints shall be preponderance of the evidence."
Section 1.4: "This policy governs all complaints arising from conduct that occurred during the effective period of this policy."

**Google Doc — "BSU Title IX Policy v6.0" (effective August 1, 2025)**
Section 8.2: "The standard of evidence for all formal complaints shall be clear and convincing evidence."
Section 1.4: "This policy governs all formal complaints filed on or after August 1, 2025, regardless of when the underlying conduct occurred."
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @provost.williams, July 15, 2025]: "Legal counsel recommends 'filed on or after' language to align with DOE guidance. Faculty Senate approved 6-1 in closed session June 30."

**Slack — #title-ix-deputies (Sep 22, 2025, 11:17 AM)**
@diana.marchetti: Quick clarification for everyone — Case 0298 and similar transitional matters: v6.0's effective-date language controls. If the formal complaint was filed after 8/1, we use clear and convincing regardless of incident date. I know this feels counterintuitive but that's what legal and Faculty Senate approved.
@mark.innis: Even if respondent's advisor argues due process concerns about retroactive standard changes?
@diana.marchetti: Yes. The standard applies to the adjudication process, not the conduct itself. It's procedural not substantive. But flag any pushback to me directly.
[thumbs-up reaction from @rachel.ogunyemi, @mark.innis]

**Email — Subject: "Pre-hearing objection — Case IX-2025-0298" (Feb 12, 2026)**
From: respondent-advisor@studentrights.org
To: titleix@brightpath.edu, hearing-panel@brightpath.edu
CC: provost.williams@brightpath.edu
"...we formally object to the application of the clear and convincing standard. The alleged conduct occurred in March 2025, when BSU's operative policy (v5.3) applied preponderance. Retroactive application of a higher evidentiary standard to pre-existing conduct violates fundamental due process and OCR guidance..."

**PeopleSoft HR — Faculty Senate Records**
Meeting: June 30, 2025 | Quorum: Yes (6 of 9 present)
Agenda item 4: "Title IX Policy revision — evidentiary standard"
Vote: 6-1 (2 absent, 1 abstention recorded as absent per bylaws)
Minutes: NONE FILED (Secretary position vacant June-August 2025)
question: The hearing panel asks the Title IX Coordinator to clarify which evidentiary standard applies to Case #IX-2025-0298. What is the correct determination?

contributor.name: Diana Marchetti
contributor.title: Title IX Coordinator
contributor.domain_expertise: Due process requirements, procedural versioning (pre/post 2022 regs), evidence standards, cross-campus jurisdiction

choices: Clear and convincing evidence — because v6.0 Section 1.4 explicitly governs complaints filed after August 1, 2025, the formal complaint was filed September 19, 2025, and this was a deliberate procedural choice approved by Faculty Senate and legal counsel.
The determination cannot be made until the Faculty Senate minutes are located, because the policy change may not have been properly ratified given the vacant secretary position and missing minutes.
Preponderance of the evidence — because the conduct occurred under v5.3's effective period and applying a higher standard retroactively violates due process protections for the respondent.
Preponderance of the evidence — because the respondent's advisor raised a timely objection and OCR guidance prohibits retroactive changes to evidentiary standards.
